title: Faraj ibn Ismāʿīl, the amir's elder brother, takes his first wife, Shamʿa, of a ruling house of the central Sahara
source: save of 16 June 1355 (treaty record); who married is Trent's account

title: Ismāʿīl ibn Ismāʿīl, the amir's brother, is betrothed to a daughter of the Aydınids of Anatolia
source: save of 16 June 1355 (treaty record); who married is Trent's account

title: Work begins on a local governor's seat at Qurṭuba, the old capital, whose road to Gharnāṭa still stands
source: Trent's account (about 250 days before the seating on 15 March 1355; the day is approximate)

title: The amir marries his Marīnid bride, Duʿāʾ, fulfilling the betrothal agreed with the house of Fās in January 1348
The amir marries his Ḥafṣid bride, Tizemt, fulfilling the betrothal agreed with Tūnis in July 1345: his third wife, and his second bride from the Maghrib in three months
